restriction: Elf heritages only; taken at 1st level only and never retrainable in or out. The text warns you typically can't take a heritage that depends on an elven feature you lack (Ancient Elf's multi-century lifespan being the named example). content.heritages also contains 'aon-half-elf' with ancestryId 'elf' — that is the legacy half-elf heritage and should NOT be offered here.
effect: You gain the benefits of the chosen ELF heritage on top of your aiuvarin heritage (its senses, speeds, skill/feat grants — e.g. Cavern Elf darkvision, Seer Elf innate detect-magic, Ancient Elf's multiclass dedication).
evidence: "You gain the benefits of the elf heritage of your elven parent or ancestors. You typically can't select a heritage that depends on or improves an elven feature you don't have."
engineNote: BuildState has a single heritageId, so there is no slot to hold a SECOND heritage and no code path that applies a second heritage's DefenseGrants/effectChoices. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS already keys an entry off build.heritageId ('ancient-elf'), which is precedent for heritage-driven pickers — but that grants a FEAT, not a whole heritage. Needs a secondary-heritage slot whose grants merge like the primary's. Note the recursion risk: picking Ancient Elf here also drags in its own multiclass-dedication picker.
question: Elf Atavism's legal heritage list is explicitly GM-adjudicated ("at the GM's discretion, you might gain a different benefit"). Offer all 8 elf heritages including Ancient Elf (which chains into a multiclass-dedication picker), or curate the list down to the ones with no elven-feature dependency?

name: Combat Reading
reasonIfNo: In-play: the target enemy is chosen each time the 1-action ability is used, and the outcome is a GM secret roll.
evidence: "The GM rolls a secret check for you against the Deception or Stealth DC (whichever is higher) of an enemy of your choice who is not concealed from you"

name: Earworm
reasonIfNo: The cantrip is chosen during a 10-minute exploration activity and is re-chosen every time you implant a new earworm ("Allies forget the earworm … if you spend 10 minutes to implant another earworm, or during your next daily preparations"). It is a repeatable in-play selection from composition cantrips the character already knows, not a permanent build decision.
evidence: "Choose a composition cantrip and spend 10 minutes repeating a melody, chant, speech, series of motions, or a similar performance that embodies that cantrip."

name: Advanced Domain
restriction: Only domains for which you ALREADY have the initial domain spell (i.e. domains you took with Domain Initiate) — not simply every domain your deity offers. maxTakable is null, so it repeats; each taking must yield a different advanced domain spell.
effect: Grants that domain's ADVANCED domain focus spell and expands your focus pool by 1 (focusPoolBonus: 1 is already on the record).
evidence: "You gain an advanced domain spell from one of your domains for which you have an initial domain spell."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) src/rules/domains.ts has only DOMAIN_SPELLS (domain → INITIAL focus spell); there is no ADVANCED_DOMAIN_SPELLS table, so a picked domain resolves to no spell. The advanced spells do ship (competitive-edge, eradicate-undeath, tempest-form …) — this is an authoring job mirroring the existing table. (2) kind:'domains' resolves options from the DEITY's domain list; here the legal set is the subset actually taken via Domain Initiate, so the domains resolver needs a 'restrict to domains you already have an initial spell for' mode.

name: Ebb and Flow
reasonIfNo: In-play: both creatures are chosen at the moment the 1-action spellshape is used, immediately before casting heal/harm.
evidence: "choose one creature in range that would be harmed by the spell, and choose another creature within range that would be healed by the spell"

name: Divine Apex
reasonIfNo: Both halves are DAILY-PREPARATION choices, re-made every day: which worn magical item is touched, and which of the deity's divine attributes it boosts. The item can change day to day, so pinning it at build time would be wrong.
evidence: "When you complete your daily preparations, you can touch one worn magical item that doesn't have the apex trait. It gains the apex trait until your next preparations, and you choose one of your deity's divine attributes."
openSource: one of your deity's divine attributes (an attribute, restricted by deity)
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) DATA: deities carry no divine-attribute field — only 1 of 485 deity records mentions 'Divine Attribute' anywhere (surveyors-of-the-deep, in prose). Authoring that per-deity field is a prerequisite for any correct picker. (2) LANE: the closest existing mechanism is the per-item `item.apexAttribute` field in ItemEditorModal, which a player can set by hand; there is no play-state daily assignment and no enforcement of 'only one apex item at a time' against a temporarily-apex item.
question: Divine Apex needs per-deity 'divine attribute' data that core.json does not have (1/485 deities mention it). Author that field across the deity list and add a daily Play-tab apex picker, or leave the feat descriptive and let players set item.apexAttribute by hand in the item editor?

name: Echoing Channel
reasonIfNo: In-play: the extra creature is chosen at the moment the 1-action spellshape is used, right before the heal/harm resolves.
evidence: "If the next action you use is to cast a 2-action Harm or Heal to heal or damage a single creature, choose one additional creature in range."

name: Order Explorer
restriction: Must be an order OTHER than your own (exclude build.subclassId). maxTakable is null — repeatable, and each taking must pick a different order not already explored.
effect: You count as a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites, AND you gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite. You gain none of the order's other benefits (no order spell, no order skill).
evidence: "Choose an order other than your own. You gain a 1st-level feat that lists that order as a prerequisite, and you are now a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites."
engineNote: Three parts. (1) The order-membership flag for prerequisite checking has no lane. (2) The granted feat is a SECOND, dependent pick — 'a 1st-level feat whose prerequisite names the order you just chose'. FEAT_PICK_GRANTS filters by category/level/trait only, never by another choice's value, so the pool must be computed at build time. (3) DATA GAP: of the 9 orders, only 7 have a level-1 order-prerequisite feat in core.json (fire-lung/flame, shore-step/wave, steadying-stone/stone, animal-companion/animal, leshy-familiar/leaf, storm-born/storm, untamed-form/untamed). Cultivation and Spore orders have only 6th-level feats (hedge-prison, fungal-exhalation), so picking those two would grant nothing.

name: Leshy Familiar Secrets
reasonIfNo: The pick is a DAILY familiar-ability selection ("one additional familiar ability each day"), and familiar abilities are already chosen in the Companions tab, not the builder. Adding a builder prompt would duplicate that picker.
evidence: "You can select one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following leshy familiar abilities. You can't select more than one ability from this feat at a time."
engineNote: All three abilities ship in content.familiarAbilities. The gap is budget + gating, not a builder choice: deriveFamiliar in src/rules/companions.ts consumes cfg.abilities as a free list with no cap, and companionGrants.abilityBudget is documented as "a display hint — the picker itself is not hard-capped". So today these three are offered to EVERY familiar and this feat grants nothing extra. Correct fix is a familiar ability-budget model (+1 restricted slot, restricted to these three, mutually exclusive) in the Companions tab.

name: Order Magic
restriction: Only orders you actually selected with Order Explorer — the static list above is the full superset and MUST be narrowed at build time. maxTakable is null; each taking must pick a different explored order.
effect: Grants that order's INITIAL order focus spell and expands the focus pool by 1 (focusPoolBonus: 1 is already on the record). The mapping already exists in data: classes.druid.subclass.options[].focusSpells — animal→heal-animal, cultivation→cornucopia, flame→wildfire, leaf→cornucopia, spore→mushroom-patch, stone→crushing-ground, storm→tempest-surge, untamed→untamed-shift, wave→rising-surf.
evidence: "Choose an order you have selected with Order Explorer. You gain the initial order spell from that order."
engineNote: The legal option set is the set of Order Explorer picks — a cross-feat dependency that FeatChoiceDef.options (a static array) cannot express. Needs a dynamic option source reading the Order Explorer selections, plus wiring the picked order's focusSpells entry into the focus-spell grant. Build this after order-explorer; alone it would offer orders the character never explored.

name: Snowdrift Spell
reasonIfNo: In-play: the affected creature (and therefore which squares fill with snow) is selected at the moment the 1-action spellshape is used.
evidence: "If your next action is to Cast a Spell that has the air, water, or cold trait … select one creature affected by the spell on the ground."

name: Reactive Transformation
reasonIfNo: In-play: this is a reaction whose shape is chosen per trigger, and WHICH list you choose from is dictated by the triggering damage type. Nothing is fixed at build time.
evidence: "**Trigger** You take fire damage — **Effect** Choose a fire elemental shape from Elemental Form."
engineNote: The prerequisite chain (Untamed Form plus Dragon/Elemental/Plant/Soaring Shape) determines which triggers are live, but that is prerequisite evaluation, not a choice.

name: Advanced Weapon Training
restriction: One weapon group. Values are the 17 ids in content.weaponGroup. The text imposes no restriction, but only 13 groups actually contain advanced weapons in shipped data (axe 5, sword 22, firearm 9, knife 5, club 4, flail 10, crossbow 3, dart 2, sling 3, bow 3, pick 2, spear 1, polearm 2) — bomb, brawling, hammer and shield would be inert picks.
effect: Every ADVANCED weapon in the chosen group uses your MARTIAL weapon proficiency rank instead of your advanced rank (attack rolls, and it feeds crit-spec/rank-scaling the same way).
evidence: "Choose a weapon group. You gain proficiency with all advanced weapons in that group as if they were martial weapons of their weapon group."
engineNote: No lane. BuildState.fighterWeaponGroup exists but is bespoke to Fighter Weapon Mastery/Legend (it pushes a group to master@5/legendary@13). FeatGrant.weaponFamiliarity takes a STATIC weapon list plus a flat rank or mirrorBestCategory — mirrorBestCategory is too generous here (it mirrors the best category rank, not specifically martial). Needs a 'group → treat advanced as martial' override applied through the same weaponOverrides path deriveStrike already reads.

name: Determination
reasonIfNo: In-play: the condition/spell/effect being shrugged off is chosen at the moment the once-per-day 1-action ability is used, from whatever is currently afflicting you.
evidence: "Choose a single nonpermanent condition, spell, or magical effect that is affecting you."

name: Double Prey
reasonIfNo: No choice is made when the feat is taken. It only widens the Hunt Prey ACTION to two targets, and those targets are chosen in play each time Hunt Prey is used.
evidence: "When you use the Hunt Prey action, you can pick two creatures as your prey."
engineNote: HH models hunt-prey as a boolean whileActive state (DefenseGrants.whileActive state 'hunt-prey'), so nothing in the derivation changes whether one or two creatures are marked — the feat is correctly inert in the build layer.

name: Sabotage
reasonIfNo: In-play: the sabotaged item belongs to a target creature in reach and is chosen at the moment the action is used.
evidence: "Choose one item that a creature within your reach wields or carries. The item must have moving parts that you could possibly sabotage"

name: Rites of Convocation
openSource: any summon spell that appears on your spellcasting tradition's list
restriction: Must be a 'Summon …' spell on the tradition of your witch spellcasting. 27 summon spells ship, e.g. summon-animal (r1, arcane/primal), summon-construct (r1, arcane), summon-fey (r1, occult/primal), summon-undead (r1, arcane/divine/occult), summon-elemental (r2, arcane/primal), summon-dragon (r5, all four), summon-kaiju (r10, primal).
effect: Names a permanent 'convocation' spell. Thereafter, 10 minutes of communion with your familiar swaps one prepared witch spell for the chosen summon spell, heightened to the replaced slot's rank; the replaced slot must be at least the summon spell's minimum rank.
evidence: "Choose one summon spell (such as Summon Animal, Summon Construct, and so forth) that appears on the spell list of your spellcasting tradition."
engineNote: The PICK is build-time and permanent; the EFFECT is a prepared-slot flexibility the engine cannot express. SpellChoiceFilter.grantAs offers only 'innate' | 'focus' — neither is right (this spell is cast from a witch slot with witch statistics). Also, 'summon spell' is not a trait in the data: the 27 spells are identifiable only by the 'Summon ' name prefix, so the filter needs a name/id list rather than a trait match. Minimum viable = record the pick for display (an EffectChoice option with no grant already supports a grant-less recorded pick).
question: Rites of Convocation's benefit is a 10-minute prepared-slot SWAP, which the spell-slot model does not support. Is recording the chosen summon spell for display (and letting the player do the swap by hand on the Spells page) acceptable, or should a 'flexible swap' lane be built?

name: Incredible Familiar
reasonIfNo: Nothing is chosen when the feat is taken — it only raises the DAILY familiar/master ability budget from four to six. The abilities themselves are already selected in the Companions tab.
evidence: "You can select a base of six familiar or master abilities each day, instead of four. **Special** Add the bonus familiar abilities you gain for being a witch to this amount."
engineNote: Currently inert. deriveFamiliar (src/rules/companions.ts) treats cfg.abilities as an uncapped list, and companionGrants.ts documents abilityBudget as "a display hint — the picker itself is not hard-capped"; its header explicitly excludes Enhanced/Incredible Familiar on the grounds that "the existing Companions UI handles them". To make this feat matter, the familiar picker needs a real budget (base 4, +2 from this feat, +witch bonus, +1 restricted from Leshy Familiar Secrets) shown and enforced.

name: Tyrant's Writ
reasonIfNo: The four benefits (Bloody / Explosive / Necrotic Speed / Rotten) are picked at activation time, once per day, and apply to a specific undead the character just animated. Nothing is fixed when the grimoire is bought, so a builder prompt would store a value that is wrong the moment the item is used again.
evidence: "Frequency once per day; Effect If your next action is to Cast a Spell to cast an animate dead spell prepared with tyrant's writs, you can choose one of the following additional benefits to grant the summoned undead."
engineNote: The four benefits modify a summoned undead creature, which the app does not model as a companion/creature entity; even in-play there is nothing for the engine to attach them to. The record already carries the frequency text but no `counters` entry for the once-per-day use, unlike the other frequency items in this chunk.

name: Oozepick
reasonIfNo: The record contains no 'choose' language of any kind. It is a consumable that becomes a set of thieves' tools with a flat +2 item bonus to Thievery for Pick a Lock / Disable a Device against one mechanism. The only variable (which lock it is poured into) is an in-play target.
evidence: "The ooze is treated as a set of thieves' tools that last for 1 hour and provide a +2 item bonus to Thievery checks to Pick a Lock or Disable a Device against the mechanism into which they were first poured."

name: Oozepick (Greater)
reasonIfNo: Identical to the base Oozepick with a longer duration and a larger bonus; no choice language anywhere in the record. The mechanism it is poured into is an in-play target.
evidence: "The ooze is treated as a set of thieves' tools that last for 8 hours and provide a +3 item bonus to Thievery checks to Pick a Lock or Disable a Device against the mechanism into which they were first poured."

name: Library Robes
openSource: Any spell you know (repertoire, prepared list, or otherwise available to you) of 5th rank or lower
restriction: Rank 5 or lower, and it must be a spell the character knows. You must pay the minimum materials to Craft a scroll of that spell (about half a scroll's Price plus any extra cost); no Crafting proficiency and no Magical Crafting feat needed. Re-chosen at each daily preparation, and choosing erases the previous inscription.
effect: Puts a single-use scroll of the chosen spell on the character (naturally the Spells page, as an item-held spell with 1 charge), on top of the robes' baseline +1 resilient scroll robes statistics.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one spell you know of 5th rank or lower. You inscribe that spell on the robes ... Using this ability erases any scroll already inscribed on the robe."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) NO item in core.json currently carries a `choice` field (verified: 0 of the whole items collection), so the choice lane is feats/classFeatures-only today — item-borne choices need an engine path that reads `choice` off an owned item instance and stores the answer per item copy, not per character. (2) The answer must materialise as a one-use spell entry: the app already has `heldSpells` + `inv.counters` charges for staves/wands, so the plumbing exists, but `heldSpells` is a static authored map — it cannot currently be filled from a player answer. (3) The option pool is character-dependent ('a spell you know'), so the picker must read the character's own repertoire/prepared list rather than the global spell list.
question: Library Robes is re-chosen at every daily preparation, not locked at purchase. Should re-selectable daily-prep choices like this live in the builder `choice` lane (answer persisted on the item, editable any time), or in the play state alongside the existing alchemist Advanced-Alchemy daily prep? The same call decides the other three Library Robes grades and every 'during your daily preparations, choose' item.

name: Library Robes (Greater)
openSource: Any spell you know (repertoire, prepared list, or otherwise available to you) of 6th rank or lower
restriction: Rank 6 or lower, and it must be a spell the character knows. You must pay the minimum materials to Craft a scroll of that spell; no Crafting proficiency and no Magical Crafting feat needed. Re-chosen at each daily preparation, erasing the previous inscription.
effect: Puts a single-use scroll of the chosen spell on the character (Spells page, item-held spell with 1 charge), on top of the robes' baseline +2 resilient scroll robes statistics.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one spell you know of 6th rank or lower."
engineNote: Same as base Library Robes: no item in core.json carries `choice` today, `heldSpells` cannot be populated from a player answer, and the pool is the character's own known spells. Only the rank cap (6) and the base runes differ.
question: Same owner call as base Library Robes: does a daily-preparation re-choice belong in the builder `choice` lane or in play state?

name: Library Robes (Major)
openSource: Any spell you know (repertoire, prepared list, or otherwise available to you) of 8th rank or lower
restriction: Rank 8 or lower, and it must be a spell the character knows. You must pay the minimum materials to Craft a scroll of that spell; no Crafting proficiency and no Magical Crafting feat needed. Re-chosen at each daily preparation, erasing the previous inscription.
effect: Puts a single-use scroll of the chosen spell on the character (Spells page, item-held spell with 1 charge), on top of the robes' baseline +2 greater resilient scroll robes statistics.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one spell you know of 8th rank or lower."
engineNote: Same as base Library Robes: no item `choice` lane exists, `heldSpells` is authored-static, and the pool is character-dependent. Only the rank cap (8) and the base runes differ.
question: Same owner call as base Library Robes: does a daily-preparation re-choice belong in the builder `choice` lane or in play state?

name: Library Robes (True)
openSource: Any spell you know (repertoire, prepared list, or otherwise available to you) of 9th rank or lower
restriction: Rank 9 or lower, and it must be a spell the character knows. You must pay the minimum materials to Craft a scroll of that spell; no Crafting proficiency and no Magical Crafting feat needed. Re-chosen at each daily preparation, erasing the previous inscription.
effect: Puts a single-use scroll of the chosen spell on the character (Spells page, item-held spell with 1 charge), on top of the robes' baseline +3 greater resilient scroll robes statistics.
evidence: "During your daily preparations, choose one spell you know of 9th rank or lower."
engineNote: Same as base Library Robes. Note this record's text also still says "half the Price of a scroll of that level" where the other three grades say "of that rank" — a leftover pre-remaster wording in the source data, not a mechanical difference.
question: Same owner call as base Library Robes: does a daily-preparation re-choice belong in the builder `choice` lane or in play state?

name: Anathema Fulu
reasonIfNo: The trait is picked at activation, when the four fulu pieces are placed, and the whole item is consumed in that use. The right pick depends on what creature is being fought, so it cannot be settled in the builder; storing one would be stale on the next purchase.
evidence: "Choose one of the following traits when activating the fulus: celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, monitor, or undead."
engineNote: If the app ever wants to record it, this is the cleanest candidate in the chunk for an in-play activation prompt (a closed six-value list): celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, monitor, undead. Its effects (Sickened 2 on a failed save in the area, a -2 penalty to a later Banishment) all land on enemies, so nothing is computed on the character sheet either way.

name: Mindlock Shot
reasonIfNo: Stride vs Strike is picked when the ammunition is fired, and it dictates what the struck enemy must do on its next turn. Purely an in-play, per-shot decision against a specific target.
evidence: "When you command this ammunition, you pick a Stride or Strike."

name: Captivating Score
reasonIfNo: The emotion (Positive / Negative), the subject of the composition, and the optional instrument are all fixed when the missive is composed, so they are properties of that one written copy rather than of the character — and none of them feed any value the app computes. The effect is a one-step attitude shift on listeners, which is GM-adjudicated narrative state, not sheet math.
evidence: "You choose one of the emotions described below and write a musical composition to convey that emotion about a subject of your choice, typically a person or group."
question: Captivating Score's Positive/Negative (and its subject and instrument) are baked into each written copy but change nothing the engine calculates. Do consumables whose choice is pure flavour/record-keeping deserve a stored per-copy note field, or should the app stay silent on them? Answering this once covers a whole family of 'compose/inscribe it this way' consumables.
engineNote: "You must be trained in Performance to properly compose this missive (or trained in an appropriate Lore skill your GM allows)" is a crafting prerequisite, not a choice — it would only matter if the app gated Crafting by prerequisite skill.

name: Blending Brooch
reasonIfNo: The only choice is which visible creature you become invisible to, made when the talisman triggers on a Stealth initiative roll. An in-play target selection on a consumable talisman.
evidence: "When you Activate the talisman, choose one creature you can see. You become invisible to that creature unless it succeeds at a save."
engineNote: Unrelated to choices, but flagging a data mismatch in the record: the description says "**Activate** ⟨4⟩" (a reaction, matching the Trigger line) while `activationCost` is `{type:'free'}`. Talisman activations are free actions per the talisman rules, so the description glyph looks like the wrong one.

name: Whelming Scrimshaw
reasonIfNo: The single choice is which creature within 30 feet to target when the item is broken; it is consumed in that use. Amphibious and aquatic creatures being immune is a condition on the target, not a player option.
evidence: "When you Activate this item, you break it and choose one creature within 30 feet."

name: Beguiling Crown
reasonIfNo: All three activations pick a target or resolve automatically in play; the wearer never locks anything in at build time. Even the wording that looks like a build choice — increase Charisma by 1 or set it to +4 — is not a choice: it says "whichever would give you a higher value", so the better of the two is forced.
evidence: "Effect Choose one living creature within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed at a saving throw or become helpful to you for the next 24 hours."
engineNote: The Charisma apex is already handled by `apexAttribute: 'cha'`. Two passive effects in the text have no representation in the record and are not choices, so they are out of this pass's scope but worth noting: the automatic one-step attitude improvement for creatures within 30 feet, and the -4 status penalty to the wearer's Perception DC against Deception (a genuine, always-on numeric penalty to the sheet).

name: Tome of Restorative Cleansing
reasonIfNo: The only choice is which already-healed creature receives the temporary Hit Points, decided in play immediately after the qualifying spell resolves. This umbrella record also carries no Price and no `counters`; it is the AoN combined entry whose real statistics live in the three graded records.
evidence: "Effect Choose one creature whose condition was removed by the required spell."
engineNote: This base record is a combined AoN entry (level 5, no price, all three grades concatenated into one description, no `counters` block) that duplicates the lesser/moderate/greater records. Nothing to do for choices, but it is likely a buyable duplicate in the item list.

name: Tome of Restorative Cleansing (Lesser)
reasonIfNo: Choosing which creature gets the 1d8 temporary Hit Points happens in play, immediately after the grimoire-prepared spell removed that creature's condition. The candidate set is defined by what just happened at the table, so no build-time prompt can populate it.
evidence: "Requirements Your last action was to cast a spell prepared from this grimoire ... Effect Choose one creature whose condition was removed by the required spell."

name: Tome of Restorative Cleansing (Moderate)
reasonIfNo: Same in-play target choice as the lesser grade, only the temporary Hit Points scale (2d8). The eligible creature is determined by the spell that just resolved.
evidence: "Effect Choose one creature whose condition was removed by the required spell ... that creature gains 2d8 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour."

name: Tome of Restorative Cleansing (Greater)
reasonIfNo: Same in-play target choice as the other grades, only the temporary Hit Points scale (3d8).
evidence: "Effect Choose one creature whose condition was removed by the required spell ... that creature gains 3d8 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour."

name: Cube of Recall
reasonIfNo: Attuning a side means standing in a place during play and spending 10 minutes; the 'options' are campaign locations that exist only in the GM's world, so there is no enumerable pool and nothing the engine could compute from an answer. Which side to press is likewise an in-play decision.
evidence: "Effect Pick one side of the cube and set it face up. You attune the cube to the location you currently occupy."
engineNote: Not a choice, but a plausible future nicety: six free-text slots on the item instance so the player can name what each side is attuned to (black, white, four greys). That is journaling/UI, not a rules choice, and no existing field would consume it.

name: Ghost Lantern
reasonIfNo: The only choice is made by whoever is standing in the light — and only in the corner case where their weapon already has the maximum property runes — deciding which rune to suppress for ghost touch. That is per-creature, per-activation, and can apply to allies rather than the lantern's owner.
evidence: "If an affected weapon or attack is magical and already has the maximum number of property runes, the wielder can choose one to suppress to gain ghost touch."
engineNote: If the app ever wants the owner's own weapons to reflect this, it would need a temporary rune-suppression/substitution overlay on equipped weapons (grant ghost touch, suppress one existing property rune for 5 minutes). That is a Modes-style toggle, not a builder choice — and only worth building if item-granted temporary rune effects become a general lane.

name: Bewitching Bloom (Amaranth)
reasonIfNo: The only choice is which willing ally within 30 feet to target, made at activation. The benefit lands on the ally, not the wearer, so there is nothing on the character's own sheet for a stored answer to drive.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet. The ally feels impervious, immortal."

name: Bewitching Bloom (Bellflower)
reasonIfNo: Target-an-ally at activation. The follow-on decision — re-save against a condition versus spending a reaction to Escape — is also made in play by that ally, based on which conditions they currently have.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... the target can attempt a new save against a condition the bonus applies to, or they can use a reaction to attempt to Escape"

name: Bewitching Bloom (Cherry Blossom)
reasonIfNo: Target-an-ally at activation; the recovery-check DC change applies to that ally for 1 minute. Nothing is fixed when the tattoo is acquired.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... any recovery checks the ally attempts have a DC of 10 instead of 10 + the ally's dying value."

name: Bewitching Bloom (Lilac)
reasonIfNo: Target-an-ally at activation; the ally then makes a Recall Knowledge check with a +2 status bonus. Both the target and the knowledge check are in-play events.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... The ally attempts to Recall Knowledge with a +2 status bonus"

name: Bewitching Bloom (Lotus)
reasonIfNo: Target-an-ally at activation; the +2 (or +3 vs emotion) status bonus to Will saves against mental effects is granted to that ally for 1 minute.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... The ally gains a +2 status bonus to Will saves against mental effects for 1 minute."

name: Bewitching Bloom (Purple Iris)
reasonIfNo: Target-an-ally at activation; the bloom then casts a fixed 5th-rank Command (DC 28) whose own targets are chosen in play. The spell and its rank and DC are all fixed by the item, so there is no build-time selection.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... The bloom casts a 5th-rank Command spell (DC 28) selecting targets within range of the ally."

name: Bewitching Bloom (White Poppy)
reasonIfNo: Two choices, both at activation: which willing ally to target, and Calm versus Sanctuary. The spell pick depends on the situation at the table (Calm to shut down an aggressor, Sanctuary to shield the ally) and can differ every day, so locking it in the builder would be wrong.
evidence: "Effect Choose a willing ally you can see within 30 feet ... The tattoo casts Calm or Sanctuary (your choice) on the ally."
engineNote: Contrast with Faith Tattoo in this same chunk: there the harm/heal pick is explicitly locked "when you receive the tattoo" (build-time), whereas here the wording is a bare "(your choice)" inside the Effect block with no acquisition-time language — the deciding difference between the two.

name: Faith Tattoo

reasonIfNo: IN-PLAY. A consumable elixir: the skill you sacrifice is named when you drink it and the drawback ends with the elixir's duration (1 minute to 1 hour). Nothing persists in the build.
engineNote: If the owner wants this playable rather than prose-only, the right home is the existing Modes system (a toggleable modifier set: +N to Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation/Performance, −2 to Arcana/Crafting/Lore/Occultism/Society, one skill dropped to untrained) — which would need a per-mode skill picker, a capability Modes does not have today. Also note this base record is an umbrella AoN dump (level 1, no price) that repeats all four graded variants below; it probably should not appear in item pickers alongside them.

name: Silvertongue Mutagen (Lesser)
evidence: "Choose one skill in which you are trained; for the duration, you become untrained in that skill." **Duration** 1 minute.
reasonIfNo: IN-PLAY. Consumable activation choice with a 1-minute duration — decided at the table when the mutagen is drunk, not at build time.

name: Taper of Sanctification

reasonIfNo: The chooser is explicitly "the crafter … when the candle is made", i.e. a property of that physical candle, not a decision the owning character makes. The benefit ("that creature's Strikes gain the holy or unholy trait until the next time that creature makes their daily preparations") is also a temporary play-time state on whoever prayed, and the candle is consumed.
question: Should this ship as two variant item records — Taper of Sanctification (Holy) / (Unholy), the way item grades are already split — rather than as a choice? EffectChoice picks are keyed `<recordId>:<choiceId>`, i.e. per item DEFINITION, so a character holding one holy and one unholy taper could not be represented. Related: the candle is also "dedicated to a deity who can be sanctified to holy or unholy" — do you want the deity recorded on the item at all, or is it pure flavour?

name: Storied Skin
openSource: Any Lore subject — free text, exactly like Background.trainedLoreChoice ("the player types the subject in the builder"). Not a fixed list.
restriction: Chosen once, permanently, when the tattoo is applied — the record says "When you receive the tattoo", and the activation later refers back to "the chosen Lore skill". It is not re-picked.

engineNote: EffectChoice can only offer a fixed `options` array (or a spellFilter); there is no free-text Lore-subject input on the effect-choice lane — `trainedLoreChoice` exists only on Background. Either add a free-text/lore kind to EffectChoice, or fall back to enumerating a fixed Lore list the way ancestral-geometry does (which would wrongly exclude Lores outside that list). The bonus itself is expressible once the subject is known, and the loreBonus type comment already blesses treating a Recall-Knowledge-only Lore bonus as a flat Lore bonus.

name: Stone of Unrivaled Skill
openSource: Any skill — the text says only "one skill", with no restriction to trained skills and no list, so the pool is all skills (Lore subjects presumably included).
restriction: Chosen once when the bargained contract is sealed; permanent for as long as the contract is invested. Never re-picked.
effect: Raises that skill's proficiency ONE STEP with a floor of expert: untrained/trained → expert, expert → master, master → legendary. The same chosen skill is also what the Taste Fluency activation buffs (+3 status bonus for 10 minutes, once per day).
evidence: "Choose one skill when you seal this bargained contract. You become an expert in that skill; if you were already an expert, you become a master, and if you were already a master, you become legendary."
engineNote: Two blockers. (1) EffectGrant.skills is documented as "Skill (or lore:<subject>) → MINIMUM rank trained", so a hard-coded 'expert' grant would leave an existing expert at expert — this needs a new relative "raise one step (min expert)" grant, which no lane provides. (2) There is no all-skills picker on the choice lanes: EffectChoice takes only a fixed `options` array, and FeatChoiceDef's kind is only 'domains' | 'array' — the 'skills' kind this record needs does not exist yet. This is the single highest-value record in the chunk: it is a permanent, always-on proficiency change that the app currently drops entirely.

The bonus increases to +3 when the relic is 17th level"). ItemPassiveEffects.skills is a flat number with no level table, and the app has no notion of a relic's level as distinct from the character's. Also unhandled: taking the gift twice (EffectChoice ids are single-pick per record). Verify the shipped choice before adding anything — do not duplicate it.

restriction: Exactly one of the two named skills; permanent once the relic gift is gained (no re-pick clause, unlike Muse).

engineNote: The pick itself is trivially expressible (two-option EffectChoice, same shape as the sibling `muse` record which already ships one), but the EFFECT is a degree-of-success upgrade and there is no lane for it — EffectGrant/ItemPassiveEffects only carry numeric bonuses, ranks, senses, IWR, speeds and spells. Ship the two options with no `grant` plus a `note` describing the upgrade; the type comment explicitly sanctions this ("some menus mix a mechanical option with play-time ones … and the pick should still be recorded and shown", as done for kineticist gate junctions).

name: Ancestors' Call
openSource: Pool = common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats. I enumerated it from core.json: 19 level-1 dwarf ancestry feats exist, 10 of them common — the 10 options above. Enumerating is safe here, but the list must be regenerated if dwarf feats are added.
restriction: Common, 1st-level, dwarf, ancestry feats only; three distinct picks; locked in "when you gain this gift".
effect: NOTHING is permanently gained. The three picks are a loadout: on each activation (once per hour) you "Select one of the three ancestry feats" and you plus allies in a 10-foot burst gain that one feat and the dwarf trait for 1 minute. So the build-time job is to record and display the three, not to grant them.
evidence: "When you gain this gift, choose three common 1st-level dwarf ancestry feats." … "Select one of the three ancestry feats. You and each ally … gain that feat and the dwarf trait for 1 minute."
engineNote: Two gaps. (1) MULTI-PICK: EffectChoice resolves to one value per choice id; three picks would need three sibling choice ids (ancestors-call-1/2/3, with de-duplication between them) or a new multi-pick shape. (2) DISPLAY-ONLY FEAT PICK: the existing feat-picking lane (featPickGrants / FEAT_PICK_GRANTS) permanently grants the chosen feat and tags it "Granted" — using it here would be WRONG, since the character never actually has these feats outside the 1-minute activation. Emit options with no `grant` so the picks are only recorded and shown on the item.

name: Born of Item
openSource: any Lore subject (free text) — the tool/object you used to be
restriction: Flavour-restricted only ("related to what kind of tool you were"); RAW imposes no closed list, so free text is correct.
effect: Trains the character in lore:<typed subject>. ALREADY EXPRESSED: the record carries loreChoices: 1, which build.ts (line ~1208) reads from BuildState.heritageLore and grants as trained, and shared.tsx (~2331) renders as a "Heritage Lore" text input. No new field needed for the training itself.
evidence: "Choose one Lore skill related to what kind of tool you were... You become trained in this skill."
engineNote: The Lore TRAINING works. What does NOT work is the follow-on: "Humanoid Form ... you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Lore skill you obtained through this heritage." FEAT_SITUATIONAL (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts) is keyed by FEAT id only and its SituationalTarget.detail is a static string, so it cannot express (a) a heritage source nor (b) a target resolved from the player's typed Lore. Two gaps: a heritage situational lane, and a dynamic lore:<chosen> target. Yaoguai Humanoid/Yaoguai Form is not modelled anywhere in src (no hits for 'yaoguai' outside two feat grant tables), so the form gate has no home either — display-only is the honest fallback.

name: Warden Human (BB)
restriction: Exactly one of the three; chosen at level 1 and never changes.
effect: hp → +4 flat to maximum HP. fortitude-expert → Fortitude save proficiency raised to expert (RAISES only; a fighter is already expert, so it would be a no-op for them). medium-armor → medium armor proficiency raised to trained.
evidence: "Pick one of the following benefits." — then "Add 4 to your maximum Hit Points", "expert in Fortitude saving throws", "trained in medium armor".
engineNote: Nothing here is expressible today, so this heritage is currently 100% inert. (1) Heritage (types.ts:475) has NO `choice` field — FeatChoiceDef/`choice` lives only on Feat (types.ts:541), and Heritage's mixin DefenseGrants carries senses/resistances/speeds/loreChoices/grantsFeats but no proficiency or HP grants. (2) Even with a choice stored, there is no heritage-side grant lane: save/armor ranks live on FeatGrant (featGrants.ts:58-62) and maxHpBonus lives on Feat (types.ts:562, consumed by featHpBonus in derive.ts:318 which iterates c.feats only) — heritages feed neither. Cheapest path that reuses existing machinery: give Heritage a `choice` + `choiceGrants` pair mirroring FeatGrant.choiceGrants (featGrants.ts:131) and let heritage grants flow through the same apply loop; that also unblocks any other "pick one benefit" heritage. A hackier alternative — three synthetic feats wired via the existing Heritage.grantsFeats — still needs a choice field to pick between them, so it saves nothing.

name: Magical Experiment

options.label: Enhanced Senses — low-light vision (darkvision if you already had low-light vision) plus a 30-foot imprecise sense
Resistant Skin — resistance equal to half your level (min 1) to two energy types
Touch Telepathy — telepathy with any creature you are touching that shares a language

restriction: The list is explicitly open-ended ('or to come up with another special ability') and GM-gated
effect: Enhanced Senses: grants low-light vision, upgraded to darkvision if the ancestry already gave low-light vision, plus a chosen imprecise sense (scent/thoughtsense/tremorsense/wavesense) at 30 ft. Resistant Skin: resistance = floor(level/2), min 1, to two of acid/cold/electricity/fire/sonic. Touch Telepathy: narrative only, no numbers.
evidence: "You gain one special ability as a result of the magical experimentation. Work with the GM to select an appropriate ability from the following list or to come up with another special ability."
engineNote: Nothing about this is expressible today. (1) Background extends only ContentBase — unlike Feat/Heritage it does NOT extend DefenseGrants, so it has no senses/resistances/effectChoices fields at all. (2) The generic 'choose one of N' lane already exists and is exactly the right shape (EffectChoice + BuildState.effectChoices + resolvePick in build.ts:2212), but resolvePick is called only for feats, heritage, class features, grant options and items (build.ts:2277-2284) — never for the background. Cheapest path: add `effectChoices?: EffectChoice[]` to Background, one resolvePick call, and a builder card on the Background panel. (3) Enhanced Senses and Resistant Skin each need a NESTED second pick (which imprecise sense; which energy type) that EffectChoice cannot express — it is a flat one-level menu. Modelling them as pre-expanded options (one option per sense / per energy type) avoids the nesting.
question: Resistant Skin says the resistance covers "two of the following types … one chosen by you and the other chosen by the GM". Should the builder let the player pick BOTH types, pick one and leave the second unset, or expose it as a GM/free-text note? And should the explicit 'or come up with another special ability' escape hatch be offered as a free-text option, or omitted (leaving it to the Homebrew section)?
